title: Heart, Lameness, and Common Diseases in Calves
text:
9. HEART - normal heart rate of cattle is 48-84 beats per minute.

What to look for?
- Arch back
- Wasting
- Recumbent
- Apathy

10. LAMENESS

What to look for?
- Abnormal walking posture and gait
- Arched back
- Favors one or more limbs to walk
- Reluctance to bear weight to the affected limb
- Recumbent

Common diseases in calves:

1. NAVEL ILL AND NAVEL ILL - swelling of the navel caused by an infection. Calves with severe infection died within 5 days.

Clinical signs:
- Fever
- Swelling of the joints
- Pus and transudate leaks out the navel

facts: The normal heart rate of cattle is 48 to 84 beats per minute.
Signs to look for regarding heart problems in cattle include arched back, wasting, recumbent state, and apathy.
Signs to look for regarding lameness in cattle include abnormal walking posture and gait.
An arched back can indicate lameness as well as heart issues.
Lame cattle favor one or more limbs when walking.
Lame cattle show reluctance to bear weight on the affected limb.
Lameness can cause cattle to become recumbent.
Navel ill is a swelling of the navel caused by an infection in calves.
Calves with severe navel ill infection died within 5 days.
Clinical signs of navel ill include fever, swelling of the joints, and pus and transudate leaking out of the navel.
